Golden State Valkyries Win First WNBA Title in Historic Game 7

01 Nov 2026, 06:03 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Sports Desk · Source: www.theguardian.com

2 min read

Key takeawaysThe Golden State Valkyries captured their first WNBA title in franchise history with a 68-63 victory over the Atlanta Dream in Game 7 of the WNBA finals at Chase Center. According to reports of the game, the victory marks a remarkably fast rise for a second-year franchise that entered the league just two seasons ago.

Second-Year Franchise Secures Championship

The Golden State Valkyries captured their first WNBA title in franchise history with a 68-63 victory over the Atlanta Dream in Game 7 of the WNBA finals at Chase Center. According to reports of the game, the victory marks a remarkably fast rise for a second-year franchise that entered the league just two seasons ago.

The decisive contest was the first Game 7 in WNBA history, following the league's recent expansion of the finals to a best-of-seven format.

Williams Leads Second-Half Surge

Finals MVP Gabby Williams scored 30 points to lead the Valkyries, with the bulk of her scoring coming during a strong second-half performance.

  • Third-Quarter Turnaround: Williams hit three consecutive three-pointers in the third quarter to help erase an Atlanta lead, scoring 15 points in the period alone.
  • Crucial Shotmaking: With two seconds remaining on the shot clock, Williams connected on a contested three-pointer to give Golden State a 60-57 lead with 2 minutes and 14 seconds left.
  • Supporting Contributions: Point guard Veronica Burton contributed a double-double with 10 points and 10 rebounds, while Tiffany Hayes added 11 points.

For the Atlanta Dream, Jordin Canada scored 18 points, Allisha Gray added 16, and Angel Reese finished with eight points and 12 rebounds.

Playoff Path to the Title

To reach the finals, the Valkyries defeated Dallas in the first round and swept the defending champion Las Vegas Aces. Entering the postseason as the No 2 seed with a 32-12 regular-season record, Golden State overcame several deficits during their playoff run, including overcoming a 2-1 series deficit against Atlanta in the finals.
